title: European Commission announces Coalition against Poverty
excerpt: The initiative will involve the private sector and philanthropy to address poverty and social exclusion across Europe.
bodyHtml:
The European Commission announced on October 16, 2026, the creation of a Coalition against Poverty. This initiative will include the private sector and philanthropy to address poverty and social exclusion, according to Executive Vice-President Mînzatu.

The Commission stated that one in five Europeans is at risk of poverty and social exclusion. This figure includes 19.3 million children, while more than 1.4 million people are homeless or do not have secure housing.

The European Commission also plans to test a European Child Guarantee Card, which is a digital tool to help children in need access the support they are entitled to. Additionally, the Council is expected to approve the Commission's proposal for a recommendation on fighting housing exclusion, which is the first EU legal act on homelessness.

The European Social Fund Plus and future National and Regional Partnership Plans are available to support Member States in making investments and structural reforms to carry out the EU Anti-Poverty Strategy.
topic: Statement by Executive Vice-President Mînzatu ahead of the International Day for the Eradication of Poverty
